text:
maya: Heads-up — saw a spike in GPU pod Pending counts during spot churn this morning. CA didn't fall back to on-demand fast enough and a couple of jobs timed out. Anyone seen similar?

jon: Yup. Came in around 07:14. Autoscaler log shows it evaluated, but NG min-size prevented immediate scale-up of the on-demand group. Warm spare nodes were still initializing.

li: Can you paste the CA snippet and the nodegroup labels? Need to check scale-up priorities.

maya: ca log snippet:
```
I0318 07:14:22 cluster_autoscaler.go:432] Scale-up request for gpu-spot-pool: 3 nodes (pending pods: 12)
I0318 07:14:27 cluster_autoscaler.go:452] Skipping nodegroup from scale up: on-demand-gpu (minSize reached)
I0318 07:15:03 cluster_autoscaler.go:501] No scale-up: resources insufficient to place pods
```
node labels: `k8s.aws/instance-type=g4dn; redwood.io/capacity-type=spot` for spot pool and `redwood.io/capacity-type=ondemand` for the fallback pool.

infra-bot: :warning: Spot eviction notice received for 3 nodes (instance-abc, instance-def, instance-ghi) at 07:13:58 — provider: aws (2m notice).

sam: Two quick ideas: (1) add a tiny on-demand warm-spare NG with minSize 1-2 and nodeSelector so CA can scale it out without violating minSize; (2) use lifecycle hooks to extend the termination window to give our drain handler time to migrate pods.

ashley: Also ensure GPU taint on spot nodes so latency-sensitive services don't schedule there. `kubectl taint nodes -l redwood.io/capacity-type=spot spot=true:NoSchedule` and rely on tolerations for batch jobs. Keeps expensive inference pods safer.

li: For lifecycle hooks, on AWS use `autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING` hook to pause termination and call the drain handler. Example:
```json
{"LifecycleHookName":"spot-drain-hook","AutoScalingGroupName":"gpu-spot-asg","LifecycleTransition":"autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING","HeartbeatTimeout":120}
```
That gives us ~2 minutes to cordon/drain and push cached KV back to persistent store.

jon: For cluster-autoscaler config, set multiple node groups with priorities and different `maxNodesTotal` weights. Also set `--balance-similar-node-groups=true` so CA prefers smaller adjustments across groups. And add `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` to avoid thrash.

maya: Question: what's our plan for pod disruption budgets? A couple of inference services have very low replicas and block draining. Should we relax PDBs for non-prod models to lower cold-start cost?

ashley: Yup, non-prod can have `minAvailable: 0` for the PDBs. For prod, use graceful eviction by setting `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` and adding `preStop` hooks to flush cache. Also consider a `priorityClass` so CA doesn't schedule critical pods onto spot nodes unless explicitly allowed.

sam: We should also leverage provider metadata to detect termination notice and trigger an immediate scale-up of on-demand pool: small controller watches `http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/spot/termination-time` (AWS) and posts a rollout to on-demand NG via ASG API. That buys us time.

li: Ops checklist I'm proposing: 
- Add 1-2 node warm-spare on-demand NG across AZs (min 1)
- Set spot nodes tainted with `spot=true:NoSchedule` and batch tolerations
- Implement ASG lifecycle hook + drain controller (120s)
- CA config: nodegroup priorities + balance-similar-node-groups=true
- Relax non-prod PDBs and add preStop flush for prod
- Instrument cost dashboard to show spot % vs on-demand for GPU usage

jon: +1. Also add a short synthetic test that triggers eviction in staging and measures time-to-ready for fallback.

maya: I'll make a PR with CA config and a KEP for the lifecycle hooks/drain controller. Assigning owners: li for controller, ashley for taints/PDB changes, sam for ASG hook wiring.

li: I'll prototype the drain controller this afternoon. Quick design: on notice -> cordon node -> evict tolerant pods first -> annotate remaining pods so CA can consider scale-up -> wait for `HeartbeatTimeout` then complete lifecycle hook.

infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1934: "spot eviction resilience — warm spare + lifecycle hook" (link: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INFRA-1934).

maya: Thanks all. If we can get the warm-spare in before next cost review, we should reduce SLA blips while keeping spot utilization high. :thumbsup:

jon: small FYI — this will cost ~0.6x of current spot burn for the fallback nodes (rough estimate). We'll add precise numbers to the ticket.

ashley: I'll update the runbook with the drain flow and commands.

maya: Closing loop: PRs expected by EOD Wed. Ping me or @li for blockers.
